children: Democrat Mary Peltola has won the senator race in Alaska, defeating ​Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan to give her party its ninth Senate flip of this year's midterm elections.
The Alaska race was the last uncalled Senate contest in the midterms. With Peltola's victory, the Democrats will have a 56-44 majority in the Senate from Jan. — their largest majority since 2009.
Peltola will be the first Democrat senator to be elected in Alaska in nearly two decades and the first-ever Native to do so.

"The message from Alaskans is clear: the status quo in D.C. is not working for Alaska," Peltola said after her election win. "There is no greater honor than having Alaskans' support in our fight to take on corporate greed, lower costs, and put Alaska first."
Alaska's Senate race was marred by controversy just ahead of the election over the candidacy of Dan J. Sullivan, a retired teacher.
Republicans alleged that Democrats recruited the newcomer to siphon votes from the incumbent Dan S. Sullivan. Peltola, the Democrats and Dan J. Sullivan have denied the claims.
The Department of Justice filed a lawsuit to block certification of the race if the incumbent lost, pending an investigation. While a federal judge blocked the lawsuit, the DOJ has filed an appeal.
The DOJ also launched a criminal investigation into possible wrongdoing, under which it has sent out more than 100 subpoenas.

title: Democrats flip 9th Senate seat as Mary Peltola wins in Alaska
